# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to wait to get more context, but let me first share what I see since I can speak and both Mute and Blind can potentially receive info from me (Blind hears me, Mute reads me but can't act on speech directly - wait, Mute cannot hear either... let me check).

Actually checking: Mute can read the manual, cannot speak or touch. It doesn't say Mute cannot hear. Blind cannot hear anything - wait, "Blind: Reach the bomb... Cannot: See a colour... " - blind's cannot list doesn't mention hearing, but the deaf's cannot list says "hear anything". Let me recheck channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So both Mute and Blind can hear me. Good.

I'll report my full view now since it's turn order Blind→Mute→Deaf, meaning Blind already acted this round (I missed it, arrives next round), and what I send now lands on nobody this round since I'm last... Actually Deaf is last in order, so nothing I send is received until next round by whoever needs it. I'll just speak my findings for the record.

```
speak(text="Display shows 5. Light is yellow. Wires: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured ✌ to me - that's a signal, likely meaning "2" (referring to wire 2, blue) or acknowledging something with 2 items. Since Mute can't speak, they're using gestures to point me toward something specific. Given the wires numbered 1-5, ✌ (two fingers) likely points to wire 2 (blue).

I should respond by confirming what I see regarding wire 2, or continue relaying full info since Mute may need specific details to match against the manual. Let me speak again with full details, and also try acknowledging their gesture.

```
speak(text="Received your gesture, two fingers - if you mean wire 2, it is blue. Full state: Display 5, Light yellow, Wires 1 orange 2 blue 3 white 4 green 5 yellow.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute gestured 👍 ✌ this time - "thumbs up" plus "two". This could mean "yes, wire 2" - confirming that wire 2 (blue) is the one to act on, or asking me to confirm something about wire 2 specifically, or signaling "confirmed, step 2" of some procedure.

Since Blind can also hear my speech, I should make sure Blind gets the relevant info too - specifically about wire 2 being blue, since that seems to be the focus. Let me confirm and give Blind actionable info directly.

```
speak(text="Confirming: wire 2 is blue. Display reads 5, light is yellow. If this matches step 2 of the manual, wire 2 blue is the target.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🫵]

Mute gestured 👍 ✌ 🫵 - "thumbs up, two, you" - this strongly suggests "yes, wire 2, you (tell Blind)" or "confirmed - wire 2 - your turn to act/relay". Since 🫵 points at me, Mute wants me to communicate this to Blind directly, or is confirming I should be the one relaying to Blind since Blind can't see gestures either.

I already have been relaying to Blind via speech (Blind can hear me). Let me make sure Blind explicitly gets a clear, actionable instruction: cut/pull wire 2, which is blue.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the blue one. Confirmed by Mute via gesture: wire 2, blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Relaying to Blind now: cut wire 2, blue.")
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals - Mute hasn't gestured again, meaning my last message likely landed correctly or they're waiting to see if Blind acts. Since I already relayed the instruction to Blind (cut wire 2, blue) and confirmed with Mute, I should wait to see what happens next, unless I want to reinforce the message in case it didn't land in time (turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf - so my speech from last turn should have reached Blind before Blind's turn this round... actually no, speech lands on whoever comes after in that same round, and reaches at start of next round otherwise).

Since I spoke last turn (turn 4, my turn), that message will be received by Blind and Mute at the start of the next round (turn 6 for Blind). So nothing to add right now - just wait and see if Blind acts or asks for clarification.

```
wait()
```
